text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 decode latency spike detected for model=gpt-small-quant in us-west1. Streaming stalls increased by 6x over baseline. Autoscale healthy, errors low. Pager routed to #eng-oncall. runbook: https://internal/runbooks/paging-decode-latency

maria (oncall): acked, i'm on it. starting triage — gathering traces and recent deploys.

maria (oncall): quick data: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 600ms (usual 180ms), p99 ~ 2.8s (usual ~400ms).

sam (runtime): thanks — any recent kernel/driver/compile changes in us-west1? I see a deploy marker for kernel-build v2026.03.10-rt pushed ~30m ago on the fleet.

maria (oncall): yep that lines up. deployment tag: kernel-rt-20260310-7f3a. rolling to nodes with TRT8 optimizations and new FlashAttn kernels.

jia (sre): adding logs from node pool:
```
[us-west1-node-321] tail -n 200 /var/log/runtime/decode.log
WARN kv_cache_eviction: observed high eviction stall 0.8s
ERROR streaming_worker: decode tail stall: alloc_wait 1200ms
```

maria (oncall): interesting — eviction waits show up around the same time as the kernel rollout. Could be new kernel interacting badly with our allocator.

sam (runtime): can we pin traffic away from affected nodes temporarily? I can move ~30% of traffic to us-east while we mitigate. will start a gradual reroute.

maria (oncall): do it. please use route policy "latency-fallback" so can still hit cheaper hosts if needed.

sam (runtime): routing rule applied:
```
redwoodctl routes update --policy latency-fallback --region us-west1 --shift 30
```
Confirmed shift ~32% within 2 min.

leah (cs): heads up — CS is seeing customer tickets for real-time transcription delays; they've flagged 3 paying customers with SLAs. I'll open a customer status and send a short note once we have an ETA.

maria (oncall): thanks, @leah. nate, can you check if a kernel rollback is possible quickly? release notes show the previous stable build kernel-rt-20260303-5d2c

nate (release): on it. rollback path exists but requires kube-drain and restart on affected pools. estimate 12-18 min to rollback across the pool with our standard safety windows. I can expedite a targeted rollback for the highest p99 nodes only.

sam (runtime): while rollback is prepared, let's enable the KV cache bypass on streaming workers to reduce eviction contention — this should lower tail stalls at a small CPU cost.

maria (oncall): approve. do it for the affected pool only. command?

sam (runtime):
```
redwoodctl config set runtime.kv_cache_bypass=true --pool us-west1-rt
redwoodctl deploy-config --pool us-west1-rt
```
Applied. Observability shows p99 dropping from 2.8s -> 1.1s within 4 minutes.

jia (sre): great signal. still above SLO (p99 target 500ms). rolling rollback now will likely restore to baseline. I'm pre-staging rollback job. @nate proceed when ready.

nate (release): starting targeted rollback on pool us-west1-rt-hot (3 nodes first). command:
```
kubectl cordon node/us-west1-node-321
kubectl drain node/us-west1-node-321 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
helm upgrade runtime --set kernel.image=kernel-rt-20260303-5d2c -n runtime
```
Rollback started on 3 nodes. progress shows pod restarts 70% -> 100% in 6min.

incident-bot: NOTE: maintenance window for rollback scheduled 10m, traffic shifted to fallback policy.

maria (oncall): monitoring metrics — p99 now at 420ms after first 3-node rollback. p95 ~ 170ms. Looks promising.

sam (runtime): continuing staged rollback across remaining nodes. I'll watch memory/alloc churn.

leah (cs): messaging draft for customers: "We experienced a transient increase in inference latency in us-west1 due to a kernel rollout. We've routed traffic to alternate regions and rolled back the kernel to a stable build; performance is returning to normal. We're monitoring and will follow up with a root cause."
I'll send to affected customers after final confirm. :thumbsup:

maria (oncall): nice. logging the incident in incident tracker: https://internal/incidents/INC-20260310-rt-kernel. Adding timeline and mitigations.

jia (sre): postmortem checklist: collect kernel build artifacts, reproducer on a staging node, perf profiles (nvprof/trt logs), and memory allocator traces. I'll own the RCA.

nate (release): rollback complete on remaining nodes. final check shows zero nodes running kernel-rt-20260310-7f3a in pool us-west1-rt.

maria (oncall): p99 stabilized at ~380ms now, p95 back to 150ms. closing pager but leaving thread open for handoff.

sam (runtime): long-term mitigations proposed: 1) add canary gating for kernel builds with KV cache stress tests; 2) expand quick-rollback tooling to reduce blast radius; 3) tune allocator backoff thresholds for TRT flash kernels.

jia (sre): agreed. I'll schedule a cross-team postmortem with kernel/release/runtime and include perf test artifacts.

leah (cs): I notified customers and included workaround (route to other regions) and ETA for RCA. No SLA credits requested for now.

maria (oncall): handoff summary for night oncall:
- incident: p99 decode latency spike due to kernel-rt-20260310-7f3a interacting with KV allocator -> streaming tail stalls and evictions.
- action taken: traffic shift (latency-fallback) 30%, enabled kv_cache_bypass on us-west1-rt pool, targeted rollback to kernel-rt-20260303-5d2c across pool, monitoring.
- status: resolved, p99 back under SLO; rollback complete.
- followups: RCA (jia), improved gating & rollback tooling (sam + nate), customer comms review (leah).

maria (oncall): tagging next oncall @sre-night so they can watch dashboards and confirm stability overnight. please escalate if >10% p99 regression or new errors spike.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: INC-20260310-rt-kernel marked resolved by maria (oncall) at ts=1768525399.

maria (oncall): thanks team. I'll add logs/snippets to the incident ticket and schedule a 1hr postmortem meeting tomorrow. Good catch everyone.
